Further REPORT ON Mr Gensberger, French Subject, making improper suggestions
to Freida Stolk, aged 12 Years, Dutch Subject residing at No48 Bubblingwell Rd.

Made by D.S.I. Kiloh. Forwarded by Shell Sinclair

Sir,
I beg to report that Mrs Stolk, Dutch Subject, and her
daughter named Freida Stolk, aged 12 years, residing at
No 48 Bubbling Well Road, were taken to the French consulate
on the 9th July, they explained the circumstances of the
case to the French consul, who promised to interview Mr.
Gensberger, Mrs Stolk told the consul that she did not
wish to charge Mr Gensberger, but that he be ordered to pay
a certain sum of money to a Local charity. Mrs Stolk
informed me on the 23rd July that she had received two
one hundred dollar cheques from the French consul on behalf
of Mr Gensberger, one hundred dollars to be paid to The
King's Daughters Society, and one hundred dollars to be paid
to The Foreign Womens Home. Mr Gensberger, who at present
resides at No 46 Bubbling Well Road quite near where Mrs
Stolk resides, has been ordered to remove from that locality
as soon as he can obtain quarters elsewhere. These
payments are in full settlement of the charge made by
Mrs Stolk and her daughter against Mr Gensberger.

I am,
Sir,
Yours obediently,
J. C. Kiloh
D.S.I.

residing at No46 Bubblingwell Road and a Broker carrying on
business at No23 Avenue EdwardVII,met her Daughter named Freida
Stolk,aged 12 years outside No48 Bubblingwell Road,he asked the
young girl if she still collected stamps,she told him that
she did,he then asked her to come to his room for a few stamps
which she did.When they arrived in the room,Mr Gensberger who

a few stamps,he then showed her pictures of nude women,he

was relating to me what had taken place,he stated that he had
done nothing wrong,he said that he had kissed the girl but
denied touching her breasts,he did call her his sweetheart but
that that was a very common practice in his Country and that
he did not means anything by it. Mrs Stolk was very angry and

Further to Central Crime Report No. 2048.

With reference to attached Crime Report, I
have been very confidentially informed by Detective
Emelianoff, French Police, that sometime between 5 and 7
p.m., July 8th, 1929, Mr. F. M. Gensberger the owner of
Motor Car No. 1926, stopped his car in the French
Concession near Rue Lafayette where he met two Foreign
School girls aged 11 and 12 years respectively who were
playing about on the road with bicycles. Mr. Gensberger
took one of the girls into a nearby water closet and
attempted to rape her. The girl's companion ran and
informed the School Mistress who hurriedly called the
French Police but before their arrival Mr. Gensberger
ran to his car and the engine failed to start, therefore
Mr. Gensberger took to the fields and escaped. The French
Police removed the car to the French Police Station and
later the owner phoned the French Police stating that
his car had been stolen from the Bund in the International
Settlement. I understand that the French Police are taking
criminal action in the case.

Motor Car 1926 reported stolen by Mr.
Gensberger by phone at 8-30 p.m., July 8th, 1929.
